What one run of a module can cost

Source: R/core-registry-schema.R
hr_cost.Rd

The return value of a module's cost(input_stats, params) function. Counts are upper bounds for one run over the given input, except calls, which is the number of model requests expected.

Usage

hr_cost(
  calls,
  calls_max = calls,
  tokens_in_max = 0,
  tokens_out_max = 0,
  embed_max = 0,
  sends = list(),
  batched = TRUE
)

Arguments

calls

Model requests the run is expected to make.

calls_max

Model requests it can make at worst. Never taken as less than calls once costs are summed.

tokens_in_max

Prompt tokens the run sends beyond the input itself and the fixed prompt of each request: replies handed on to later merge or summary requests.

tokens_out_max

Reply tokens the run can be billed for at worst. Zero leaves it to the pre-flight check, which prices every request at input_stats$out_cap, the largest reply cap the run's model is sent. A module whose replies can exceed that states its own bound here, and the check uses the larger of the two.

embed_max

Requests to the embeddings endpoint.

sends

Input every run must send, as a list of list(tokens =, model =): a reader that sends every chunk sends at least their tokens to the model that reads them. Priced to refuse a run that cannot finish under the spending limit before it starts. NULL is the same as none.

batched

Whether requests can go out in parallel batches, which cannot be stopped part way and so are held to their worst case.

Value

An object of class hr_cost.

See also

gr_register_reader()

Examples

hr_cost(calls = 4, calls_max = 6)
#> $calls
#> [1] 4
#> 
#> $calls_max
#> [1] 6
#> 
#> $tokens_in_max
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $tokens_out_max
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $embed_max
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $sends
#> list()
#> 
#> $batched
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "hr_cost"
